pages.title: Here's What You'll Be Paying Once Your T-Mobile Plan Gets Force Migrated
key_facts: "Experience Signature Select" - 3 variants (A, B, C), differ only by price
"Experience Signature" - Military/First Responder variants up to 12 lines, starting at $66 for single lines
"Experience Signature" 55+ variants: A, B, C, D, and "TE" (Tax Exclusive)
"Experience Signature Family" variants: A, B, C, TE
"Experience More (TI)" variants: A, B, First Responder, Military, 55+ (with A and B sub-versions)
"Experience Beyond (TI)" - single main plan starting at $100 for a single line
"Experience Beyond (TI)" Military variant starting at $85 for a single line
Example given: Experience Signature Family (B), 2-8 lines starts at $132 for 2 lines, AAL price of $26 per additional line
"62 new plans" created as migration targets, all with unlimited premium data
Stated maximum price increase per line: $6
pages.content: Article describes 4 categories of new 'Experience' migration-target plans (Signature Select, Signature, More TI, Beyond TI), each with multiple lettered price variants (A/B/C/D/TE) plus segmented Military, First Responder, and 55+ versions. Feature sets by tier: Signature Select includes 60GB hotspot, Netflix with ads, 15GB Canada/Mexico, 5GB international data. Signature and More(TI) add $3 Apple TV+ promo and better trade-in values, matching the public Experience More plan's perks. Beyond(TI) adds 250GB hotspot, Hulu with ads, 30GB Canada/Mexico, 15GB international. The full row-by-row old-plan-to-new-plan mapping with every price exists only in linked downloadable files ('New Migration Plans .xlsx' and '.pdf'), NOT downloaded per read-only policy, so the complete crosswalk table itself was not captured — only the narrative description and example prices.
pages.notes: The actual crosswalk spreadsheet is a downloadable .xlsx/.pdf, not inline page content. Article states T-Mobile lowered most new-plan prices by ~$5/line between the initial announcement and this article, and that pricing/names/SOC codes are 'subject to change at any time' before July 13. Notes some legacy customers (e.g., some Simple Choice/ONE holders already losing KickBack) may not receive a migration notice at all.

pages.content: Notice page confirms current phone plan is being retired and the account moved to a new plan with a 5-year price guarantee on talk/text/5G data (taxes and fees excluded). No customer action required. FAQ accordion includes 'Why is my plan changing?', 'What does the 5-Year Price Guarantee mean?', 'Will my price change?', 'What about Price Lock or Un-contract Promise?', segment-plan (Military/First Responder/55+) question, taxes/fees question, 'What is happening to Kickback?', 'Can I keep my current plan or choose a different one?'. The 'Will my price change?' answer indicates outcomes vary — some no change, some increase — benefits carry over with additions; exact per-account impact in T-Life. Benefit tiles: Apple TV, Netflix On Us, Scam Shield, Mobile Hotspot, AAA On Us (free 1-yr AAA Classic, auto-renews).
pages.notes: Templated notice page (URL segment 'vo-b2-2026' suggests a specific customer segment); content may vary by segment code for a logged-in customer. No sign-in attempted; all content was on the public notice page.

Navigating to this URL redirected automatically to https://www.t-mobile.com/cell-phone-plans (current public plan menu). The retired legacy plan feature page no longer resolves to its own content — no '(Retired)' plan page could be captured. A redirect, not a login wall.

pages.title: Breaking: T-Mobile To Force Migrate Over 8 Million Customers To More Expensive Plans
key_facts: Headline figure: "Over 8 Million Customers"
"T-Mobile will also be increasing the cost of voice lines for these customers by $6 per line."
"Watch and tablet lines will increase by $3 per line."
"Customers with 5G Home Internet are also going to get a $6 price bump"
Example: "a ONE plan with 5 paid lines could see a $30 price increase"
Kickback example: "a price increase of $80 total" (5 lines losing $10/line Kickback credit)
T-Mobile statement (short quote): "Some customers will see no change to their monthly bill"
pages.content: Article (dated June 29, 2026, 'now official') reports T-Mobile will force-migrate Simple Choice and ONE plan customers (and possibly Magenta) off legacy grandfathered plans, affecting consumer and business accounts. Per-line increases: $6/line voice, $3/line watch/tablet, $6 for 5G Home Internet; free lines remain free. KickBack promo ending, compounding the increase. Insider discounts expected to carry over. Company statement frames it as retiring 3G/4G-era plans and moving to modern plans with a 5-year price guarantee and feature improvements, acknowledging some 'modest adjustment.' Closes noting changes take effect ~two weeks after announcement.
pages.notes: Opinion/news blog (tmo.report), not official; figures attributed to the outlet's own reporting/sources rather than an official T-Mobile press release. Predecessor to the July 1 crosswalk article.
